IS : 9047 ( Part I ) - 1978

EXPlANATORY

NOTE

Transportation by rope aerially is another type of transportation system like railways, conveyors, etc. The loads are transported by means of a carrier/carriers suspended on tensioned steel wire rope/wire ropes supported at intervals to limit sagging and thereby prevent loads from touching the ground except at planned points. This is particularly useful in regions where the facility of surmounting natural barriers gives them a great advantage over railways or roads, both of which may need heavy civil engineering work to secure easy gradients. Aerial ropeways are inexpensive to maintain; their power demand is modest It can negotiate valleys, steep and they are not seriously affected by adverse climatic conditions. grades and go in a straight line or curve and is limited only by storm conditions and visibility. In monocable units the carrying-hauling rope moves continuously at fixed/varying speeds in one The load carriers are either attached to the carrying-hauling rope by means of and/or both directions. fixed grips spaced equally at prearranged distances or by means of grips which are coupled to the In such cases the loads do not rope either automatically or manually after or before the terminals. pass round the sleeves. In bicable units the choice of a particular type depends upon the length and topography of the route, the type and intensity of the traffic, and in many cases, the relative, inaccessibility of the site, The bicable ropeways consist of two stationary carrying ropes, these being parallel to one another Under favourable and held under tension above the ground with towers suitably positioned. The vehicles have carriers with wheels arranged to conditions spans of over 300 m are possible. A separate endless moving rope is based to haul the carriers along these run on the fixed ropes. fixed ropes, the moving rope being driven and tensioned as in the case of the monocable system, In the case of bicableways of continuous type, the carriers are provided with mechanical grips which automatically attach and detach themselves from the moving rope when the carriers are leaving from or arriving at the terminal stations. In the case of bicableways of `to and fro ' type and ` jigback' type there is only one carrier per side which is gripped to the moving ropes at a preset distance. The loading in this case is affected while the carriers are stationary at the station. The terminal stations have fixed rails on which the carriers can run, these rails being structural prolonga-' tion of the fixed ropes along the route, and usually arranged to provide a connecting loop between The propulsion of the carriers along the station rails is usually the incoming and outgoing ropes. mechanized by a prolongation of the haulage rope, or by a separate slow-speed rope if the containers have to be loaded. Bicable ropeways are used where rope gradients are considerable high. Very heavy individual loads can be carried because the carrying size without materially affecting the haulage rope.
